Ask decide() to find something in an image (experimental)

Source: R/tidyllm_schema.R
field_box.Rd

field_box() is a decide() question that asks where something is in a picture. The answer is one box around it, given as four fractions of the image: top, bottom, left and right, each measured from the top-left corner (0 is the edge you measure from, 1 the far side). Multiply by the pixel height and width to crop or draw; box_to_pixels() does it for you.

Usage

field_box(.description)

Arguments

.description

What to find, as a short sentence, for example "The protest banner in photo".

Value

An S7 tidyllm_field object for use in tidyllm_schema().

Details

This feature is experimental. Only jev() answers it, the vendor labels image input and boxes as preview, and the format may change between Jev releases. openai(), gemini() and ollama() stop with a message before any request. A state without an image stops too.

A box question always returns a box, even when the thing is not in the picture. Pair it with a yes/no question that asks whether it is there, and ignore the box when the answer is no. To point at one of several images, name the image in the description: give the images names in .state and write "the dog in photo_b". Ask for one thing per box question; for several things, add several questions.

In the result, a box question is one row with type "box", answer and probability set to NA, and confidence as the model gives it (it can be NA). The columns top, bottom, left and right appear only when the schema holds a box question and are NA on all other rows. Boxes are rough for small objects in large images and their accuracy is unmeasured; check a sample by eye before you rely on them.

See also

box_to_pixels(), decide()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
questions <- tidyllm_schema(
  has_cat = field_lgl("Is there a cat in `photo`?"),
  cat = field_box("The cat in `photo`")
)
decide(list(list(photo = img("cat.jpg"))), questions, jev())
} # }
